title: Conversation Sessions for Multi-Turn Agents
dataSources: Sessions created by `SplunkAOLogger.start_session(name, external_id, metadata)` and the traces logged after it
description: Groups the traces of one conversation into a Splunk Agent Observability session with `start_session`, using `external_id` so a returning user resumes the same session.
value: Lets reviewers read a conversation in order and see where it went wrong, instead of piecing together unrelated auto-sessions, one per trace.
implementation: Call `start_session(name, external_id, metadata)` when a conversation starts, using the application's conversation id as `external_id`, then log each turn as a trace. Without it, each trace gets an automatic session.
visualization: Sessions view in the console, one row per conversation.
knownFalsePositives: Session metadata shows on the Sessions view, not in the trace detail; that is expected and not a missing-metadata problem.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

A session groups traces (one conversation). Omit it and each trace gets an auto session. `external_id` resumes a conversation.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Open the Sessions view for the stream and check that one conversation shows as one session with its traces in order.

Step 3 — Validate

Run a two-turn conversation against a test stream and confirm both traces land in one session. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Use sessions when reviewing conversations flagged by evaluators, and keep the same `external_id` scheme across services that handle one conversation.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

One session per turn: `start_session` is called per request instead of per conversation, or the LangChain invoke starts its own session (UC-13.8.7).
grandmaExplanation: We keep all the back-and-forth of one chat together, like stapling the pages of one letter, so it can be read in order.

productArtifacts.title: Start or resume a session per conversation
productArtifacts.body:
logger.start_session(
    name="support-chat",
    external_id=conversation_id,  # resumes the conversation when it returns
    metadata={"channel": "web"},
)
for user_text in turns:
    logger.start_trace(input=user_text, name="turn", metadata={"consumer": user_id})
    ...
    logger.conclude(output=answer, conclude_all=True)
